answer: Make each answer pay only in proportion to how far apart its attestors sit in the attestation graph: signatures from strangers who rarely attest the same accounts count fully, while a tight clique of mutual attestors discounts toward zero. A sybil operator's hollow flock can countersign itself all voyage long, but its signatures all trace back to one neighbourhood, like a comet that never leaves its own tail — self-attestation becomes provably worthless, and earning distant signatures means doing work strangers actually value.
